quadratic_direct.screen_notes: poly-solv is 2nd + the cos key (legend printed above cos; photo). 2nd poly-solv opens a menu (1: ax2+bx+c=0, 2: cubic). enter picks 1. Type a (screen shows a=), DOWN, b, DOWN, c (screen shows SOLVE at bottom right), enter, enter shows x1=; DOWN shows x2=. Negative numbers use the (-) key. Guide example 1,-2,2 gives x1=1+1i, x2=1-1i. For 165, -2.712, -0.0334 the guide shows no screen, so the two real roots are not shown by the guide (hand-checked: 0.024643 and -0.008213). Screens (78-page edition p.58, same example 1,-2,2): menu "POLY SOLVER 1: ax2+bx+c=0 / 2: ax3+bx2+cx+d=0"; "a=1"; "b=-2"; "c=2" with SOLVE at bottom right; "x1=1+1i"; DOWN: "x2=1-1i"; DOWN: "Store x1 / Store x2 / Quad(Ed.) f(x)?  NO YES" (stores the polynomial to f(x) for the table); DOWN DOWN RIGHT enter: vertex-form screen with SOLVE AGAIN and QUIT. r toggles the format of the solutions.

numeric_solve.screen_notes: num-solv is 2nd + the sin key (legend printed above sin). Type left side, enter, type right side, enter (guide p.58). The input screen reads "ENTER AND SOLVE / X=0.8 / SOLVE: X": every variable shows its stored value and the value you edit for the unknown IS the starting guess (video still; the person says the answer is "closer to this number"). Press enter to solve. Answer screen reads "SOLUTION / X=2.607737541 / L - R =0" with options SOLVE AGAIN and QUIT: L - R near 0 = good; use SOLVE AGAIN with a new guess to look for the other root (the photo's notebook shows both 2.607 and 3.169; how the second guess is typed is not shown: UNVERIFIED). Real example screen shows RAD and ENG: a reminder to check mode first. No lower/upper bound prompt is shown anywhere: bounds UNVERIFIED/none. Guide p.58-59 and error text "Change guess" agree. Both guide editions: no lower/upper bound field in the solver (LOWERbnd/UPPERbnd appear only for normalcdf); the SOLVE AGAIN / QUIT soft options appear on the SOLUTION screen but neither guide explains them in words. Num-solv example screens (p.57 of the 78-page edition): input screen ENTER AND SOLVE with a list of variable values and a SOLVE: line; solution screen SOLUTION / b=6.208333333 / L - R = 3.33E-10 / SOLVE AGAIN QUIT.
numeric_solve.source_loc: still: ENTER AND SOLVE screen; solution photo; guidebook p.58-59
unverified_parts: how SOLVE AGAIN takes the second guess

numeric_solve.screen_notes: Type the equation (X is ALPHA then the ) key; = sign is ALPHA CALC; an expression with no = is treated as =0). SHIFT CALC (SOLVE) asks "Y?" style prompts for each variable (type value, =), then "Solve for X" with the current value of X: type your starting value and press =. Result screen shows the equation, X= value, and L-R= (near 0 = good). Newton method: only ONE root is returned and a starting value closer to the root may be needed; if it gives up it shows "Continue: [=]". Use linear input while in SOLVE. SOLVE works in COMP mode only. Exit: AC.

numeric_solve.screen_notes: Solver (in the Equation app). Store knowns first: VARS key, RIGHT, value, EXE (manual stores B=4). Type the equation (x key, x2 key, = is SHIFT + the ( key legend, unknown is x), EXE registers it, Solve Target screen: confirm [x] and OK, then type initial value of x and EXE, make sure [Execute] is selected and EXE. Result shows the variable, its value and (Left Side)-(Right Side) (closer to 0 = better). Only ONE root is returned (Newton method); change the initial value to get another or if it fails; a Continue/Exit screen can appear. Unknown must be a letter A-F, x, y or z (no "d").
